newsitem.title: UK: Britons bet on "The English Patient" to win Oscar.
newsitem.headline: Britons bet on "The English Patient" to win Oscar.

text.p: Geoffrey Rush, Brenda Blethyn and "The English Patient" are the favourites to win Oscars at the Academy Awards ceremony in Los Angeles on March 24, British bookmakers Ladbrokes said on Tuesday.

Ladbrokes, one of the country's biggest betting shops, is offering odds of 4-5 on Rush to win the best actor award for his portrayal of a troubled pianist in "Shine" and 13-8 odds on Blethyn as best actress for her role in "Secrets and Lies".

"Geoffrey Rush has been the name on many people's lips as far as the best actor Oscar is concerned, and hundreds of our customers have backed him," Ladbrokes spokesman Simon Clare said in a statement.

"In the female category, Brenda Blethyn stands out as the one to beat after her Golden Globe success but Frances McDormand is the nominee who has been most heavily backed in our shops and she now stands at just 5-2 from 6-1," he added.

McDormand, who was nominated for her role in "Fargo", is at even odds with Diane Keaton for "Marvin's Room" while Kristin Scott Thomas for "The English Patient" stands at 5-1 and Emily Watson for "Breaking the Waves" was 8-1 in the top actress category.

"In the best film category, the most competitive category,...Ladbrokes have received thousands of pounds (dollars) for "The English Patient", now even money from 2-1, whilst "Fargo" is now 4-1 from 6-1 after substantial backing," Clare said.
"Secrets and Lies" (11-2) and "Jerry Maguire" (5-1) were also nominated for best picture.

In addition to Rush, Tom Cruise was seen as an 11-4 favourite for best actor for his role in "Jerry Maguire" followed by Ralph Fiennes at 4-1 for "The English Patient", Woody Harrleson at 7-1 for "The People v Larry Flynt" and Billy Bob Thornton at 10-1 for "Slingblade".
